findings.fix: Remove user-scalable=no (and any maximum-scale restriction) from the viewport content string.
findings.location: the viewport meta tag in the head
findings.violation: user-scalable=no disables pinch to zoom, which stops anyone who needs to zoom in from doing so.

findings.evidence: heading text "Accessibility improvements" followed by "Passengers should review the updated schedule at any station kiosk." and "Local residents may request a fare adjustment through the mobile app."
findings.fix: Rename the heading to match the schedule and fare content, or replace the paragraph text with information about actual accessibility improvements.
findings.location: the "Accessibility improvements" section, its heading and the two paragraphs under it
findings.violation: Neither paragraph under this heading is actually about accessibility; both are about checking schedules and requesting fare adjustments, so the heading misrepresents the section's content.

findings.fix: Darken the text color, for example to #595959 or the same color used for the surrounding body text.
findings.location: first paragraph of the "Accessibility improvements" section
findings.violation: Light gray text on what appears to be a white page background is low contrast and hard to read.

findings.evidence: "Updates post to the schedule page within one business day." appears in both paragraphs of the first section and again, nearly word for word, in the status card paragraph
findings.fix: Remove the repeated sentence from all but the one place it is actually relevant, or reword each paragraph so it says something new.
findings.location: first and second paragraphs of the "Accessibility improvements" section, and the status card paragraph later in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: The same boilerplate sentence is repeated three times across otherwise unrelated paragraphs, which makes the content feel templated and buries whatever is distinct about each paragraph.

findings.evidence: alt="A transit operator inspecting the platform screen doors before the morning shift."
findings.fix: Rewrite the alt text to describe what the image actually illustrates in this section, or remove the image if it does not belong here.
findings.location: the image in the "Accessibility improvements" section
findings.violation: The alt text describes a scene that has nothing to do with the surrounding paragraphs about schedule kiosks and fare adjustments, so it does not explain why the image is there.

findings.evidence: link text "read the accessibility improvements list" pointing to href="/fares/history"
findings.fix: Change the link text to describe the fare history page it goes to, or point the link at an actual accessibility improvements page.
findings.location: the sentence just before the form in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: The link text promises an accessibility improvements list but the destination is a fare history page, so a reader who follows it lands somewhere unrelated to what was promised.

findings.fix: Replace the fixed pixel width with a relative unit such as max-width:100% so the banner adapts to the viewport.
findings.location: the promo banner in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: A hardcoded 960 pixel width will overflow narrow screens, and because the page also disables zooming, a mobile reader has no way to see or reach the rest of the banner.

findings.evidence: style="height:60px;overflow:hidden" wrapping the paragraph "Riders can report a service issue through the online portal. Updates post to the schedule page within one business day."
findings.fix: Let the card grow to fit its content instead of clipping it, for example by dropping the fixed height or switching to min-height with visible overflow.
findings.location: the status card in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: A fixed 60 pixel height combined with overflow:hidden will silently cut off the paragraph text whenever it does not fit, with no scrollbar or other sign that content is missing.

findings.evidence: role="button" tabindex="0" aria-label="Delete item" wrapping an image with empty alt text
findings.fix: Move the control next to the item it acts on and give it a label naming that item, or remove it if it serves no purpose on this page.
findings.location: the delete icon control in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: The control is labeled "Delete item" but nothing nearby in the weekend service section indicates what item it deletes, so its purpose is unclear to anyone reading the page.

findings.evidence: three plain divs with class "step" reading "Choose a plan", "Enter payment details", and "Confirm your order", with no indication of which step is current
findings.fix: Mark the steps up as an ordered list and indicate the current step, for example with an aria-current attribute.
findings.location: the wizard steps block in the "Weekend service" section
findings.violation: A sequence of steps is presented as unstructured divs with no list markup and no way to tell which step the user is currently on.

findings.evidence: label for="topic-alt" reading "Route" immediately followed by a select with id="topic"
findings.fix: Change the label's for attribute to topic so it matches the select element's id.
findings.location: the Route field in the weekend service form
findings.violation: The label's for attribute references topic-alt, which does not match the select's id of topic, so the label is not actually associated with the field and clicking or reading the label will not reach it.

findings.evidence: label text "Phone number (required)" followed by input id="phone" type="tel" with no required or aria-required attribute
findings.fix: Add required or aria-required="true" to the phone input so its actual required state matches what the label says.
findings.location: the phone number field in the weekend service form
findings.violation: The label tells the reader the phone field is required, but the input itself carries no required or aria-required attribute, so that requirement is never enforced or exposed to assistive technology.

findings.evidence: input id="promo" type="text" aria-invalid="true" followed by a separate span id="s3-form-promo-error" holding the error text, with no attribute linking the two
findings.fix: Add aria-describedby="s3-form-promo-error" to the promo input.
findings.location: the promo code field in the weekend service form
findings.violation: The promo field is marked invalid but has no aria-describedby pointing at its error message, so a screen reader user focused on the field is never told what the error is.
